common_name: Flavorfall Pluot (Extra-Large Maroon-Skinned Late-Season Plum-Apricot Hybrid)

planting.note: Flavorfall is not self-fruitful and needs a compatible pollinator, such as Dapple Fire pluot or Honey Punch nectaplum, planted nearby.

directions: Flavorfall is a Zaiger Genetics interspecific plum-apricot hybrid (U.S. Plant Patent 11990, now expired) bred to extend the pluot harvest into the fall, ripening in late September to early October after most other stone fruit has finished. Fruit is extra-large with smooth maroon skin and golden flesh, with a crisp, sweet bite (around 17 Brix), and it holds well on the tree for several weeks without softening. The tree needs roughly 800 chill hours and is not self-fertile, so plant a compatible pollinizer such as Dapple Fire pluot or Honey Punch nectaplum nearby; thin the heavy fruit set in late spring for best size, and prune to an open center in the dormant season.

common_name: Flavorich Pluot (Dark Purple Late-Summer Plum-Apricot Hybrid)

planting.note: Flavorich needs a compatible pollinizer such as Dapple Dandy or Flavor King pluot, or a Japanese plum like Santa Rosa, planted nearby.

directions: Flavorich is a Zaiger Genetics interspecific hybrid originating from a cross of Friar plum with an unnamed pluot selection, producing large, dark purple-skinned fruit with firm, very sweet yellow-orange flesh. It ripens in late August to early September, roughly two to three weeks after Flavor King pluot, giving growers a mid-to-late-season option with a vigorous, upright growth habit. Trees need about 800 chill hours and are not self-fruitful, so pair Flavorich with a pollinizer such as Dapple Dandy or Flavor King pluot, or a Japanese plum like Santa Rosa or Late Santa Rosa. Thin fruit clusters in spring to improve final size, and prune annually to maintain an open canopy for good light penetration.

common_name: Flavor Finale Pluot (Amber-Red Complex-Flavored Late-Season Plum-Apricot Hybrid)

planting.note: Flavor Finale requires a compatible pollinizer such as Santa Rosa or Burgundy plum, or Flavor Grenade pluot, planted nearby.

directions: Flavor Finale (originally trialed as selection 5Z366, U.S. Plant Patent 16590) is a Zaiger Genetics plum-apricot hybrid noted for consistently topping Dave Wilson Nursery's in-house taste trials. Medium-to-large fruit has purplish-red skin over juicy amber-red flesh with a notably complex, layered flavor, and it holds on the tree from the second week of September well into October, making it one of the latest-ripening pluot selections. With a relatively low chill requirement of around 500 hours, it performs well in milder winter climates. The tree is not self-fertile and needs a pollinizer such as Santa Rosa or Burgundy plum, or Flavor Grenade pluot; the upright habit sets heavy crops that benefit from spring thinning for fruit size.

common_name: Flavorite Pluot (Sweet Red-Skinned Summer Plum-Apricot Hybrid)

planting.note: Flavorite is not self-fruitful and needs a compatible pollinizer such as Flavorfall pluot planted nearby.

directions: Flavorite is a Zaiger Genetics interspecific plum-apricot hybrid bred for exceptional sweetness, testing among the highest-Brix pluot selections at around 20 degrees Brix. Fruit is medium-to-large with red skin, and it ripens early, typically in the first two weeks of August, filling a gap between the earliest pluots and the mid-season varieties. The vigorous, semi-spreading tree needs roughly 700 chill hours and is not self-fertile, requiring a compatible pollinizer such as Flavorfall pluot planted nearby for reliable fruit set. As with other pluots, thin the fruit set in late spring to concentrate sugars and improve final fruit size.

common_name: Sweet Treat Pluerry (Plum-Cherry Hybrid, Red-Skinned Cherry-Flavored)

planting.note: Sweet Treat is not self-fruitful and needs cross-pollination from Santa Rosa plum, Burgundy plum, or Flavor King pluot planted nearby.

directions: Sweet Treat was the first named pluerry, a Zaiger Genetics interspecific hybrid predominantly of plum and sweet cherry parentage with traces of apricot and peach further back in its breeding, combining cherry-like sweetness with a plum's summery tang. Fruit is small, about the size of a ping pong ball, with red skin and yellow flesh, ripening from late June through July and able to hang on the tree for several weeks as sugars continue to build. It has a low chill requirement of roughly 200 to 300 hours, making it a good fit for mild-winter regions where many cherries fail to fruit reliably. The tree is not self-fertile and needs cross-pollination from Santa Rosa plum, Burgundy plum, or Flavor King pluot; expect a moderate, rounded tree reaching about 12 to 15 feet at maturity if left unpruned.
